newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel urges strict application of Maastricht rules.
newsitem.headline: Waigel urges strict application of Maastricht rules.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Wednesday again urged European Union members to apply strictly the Maastricht convergence criteria for participation in the planned currency union.

In a statement about a convergence report approved by Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet, Waigel said progress had been made on inflation, interest rates and currency market stabilisation, but that big corrections were needed in reducing government deficits.

"The (German) government will strictly apply the convergence criteria when the European Council decides in the spring of 1998...what member states fulfil the necessary conditions for the introduction of the euro," Waigel said.
The Maastricht Treaty calls for a high degree of sustained convergence, and the decision must take into account medium-term budget developments, he said.

"Again in 1996 there was further clear progress in stability-oriented convergence on inflation, long-term interest rates, and stabilisation of currency rates. But convergence deficits remain in the area of public finances. In this area there is still a need for major correction," he said.
European nations are to decide in about one year which countries qualify for the start of monetary union, scheduled for January 1999.
